concept: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds
summary: Source-anchored research for PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Inspect pg_index.indisvalid for query eligibility and indisready for INSERT/UPDATE maintenance; indisready=false means writes ignore the index, so invalid does not imply one universal maintenance state. (low confidence)

Deadlocks or uniqueness errors during concurrent scanning can leave invalid indexes that queries cannot use; pganalyze independently documents failed or aborted concurrent builds as a typical cause. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html ; https://pganalyze.com/docs/checks/schema/index_invalid
A unique concurrent build starts enforcing uniqueness during its second scan; failure there can leave uniqueness enforcement active even though queries cannot use the index. (medium confidence)

Retrying CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY without first dropping the leftover invalid index can fail because a relation with that name already exists (an error is thrown unless IF NOT EXISTS is given); IF NOT EXISTS only skips on a name match and gives no guarantee that the existing index is anything like the one that would have been created. The documented recovery is to drop the index and retry, or use REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY. Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html

A running concurrent build is initially invalid too; indisvalid=false alone cannot establish that creation has failed. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html

Concurrent index creation uses multiple transactions: the index is entered as invalid in the catalogs in one transaction, then two table scans occur in two more transactions. If a problem arises while scanning the table, such as a deadlock or a uniqueness violation, CREATE INDEX fails but leaves behind an invalid index. Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html

Invalid artifacts can occupy disk and incur write maintenance despite providing no query acceleration; dbi demonstrates a sequential scan and subsequent index growth. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html ; https://www.dbi-services.com/blog/create-index-concurrently-in-postgresql/

Drop and recreate a failed index, or use REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY; the latter is the REINDEX form that can concurrently rebuild an invalid index. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-reindex.html

After failed concurrent reindexing, an INVALID _ccnew artifact represents the unfinished replacement; drop it and retry. An INVALID _ccold artifact is the old index left after successful rebuilding; drop it. Numeric suffixes may follow these names. (low confidence) Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-reindex.html
